state.decision: How the Editor lets a designer author a per-character text animator (row 11.61) on codex's released contract: textObject.textAnimator = {selector{start,end,offset,amount,shape,basis,smoothness,easeHigh,easeLow,randomizeOrder}, x, y, scale, rotation, opacity?}; the edit setTextAnimator {objectIds, animator|null} (null removes it and its keys); keyable scalars textAnimator.selector.start/end/offset and textAnimator.x/y/scale/rotation/opacity through the existing editProperty path.
state.facts: Figma B3d v2 draws 'Text animator (per character) · 4 keyed rows' as a header folded under the paragraph rows. Number rows in Properties have a keyframe diamond and arrows; the text choices (Case, Align, Font...) are dropdown fields. Broadcast titles use per-character reveals (a range moving across the text while characters fade, move or scale in).
state.constraints: One undoable command per gesture; the person and agents read the same rows; nothing is offered the contract refuses (range outside 0..1, negative scale, opacity outside 0..1).

section.instructions: Where does the animator live in Properties?

criteria.A: A 'Text animator' section after the text rows, present only for text elements: an Add text animator button while there is none; once there is one, its rows and a Remove button.
criteria.B: Only in the timeline: a track menu adds an animator.
criteria.C: A separate Animator panel in the dock.

default.instructions: What does Add text animator create?

criteria.A: A neutral animator: the whole text selected, no offset, no move, scale 1, no rotation, no opacity change. Nothing changes on screen until the designer changes a row or keys one.
criteria.B: A ready-made fade by character: opacity 0 on a range that starts as a sliver at the left.
criteria.C: Ask which effect first in a dialog.

rows.instructions: Which rows does the section show?

criteria.A: Range: Start, End, Offset (percent, each with the keyframe diamond), Shape, Basis (dropdowns), Randomize order (checkbox). Change per character: Move X, Move Y, Scale, Rotation, Opacity (each with the diamond).
criteria.B: Only Offset and Opacity, the two a title designer uses most.
criteria.C: All the contract's fields including Amount, Smoothness and the two Ease values.
